source.title: Pretraining on the Test Set Is All You Need

record.tranche_reason: The paper is explicitly satire and says its benchmark figures may be made up. Its canary-prediction claim is not a test of the versions' generalization claims.
record.gate_note: The paper describes a grokking-like rise in benchmark-canary prediction, but this is a different behavior from delayed test generalization: the stated training data consists of the evaluation benchmarks themselves. The benchmark-performance and scaling claims are also explicitly presented as satire and potentially fabricated.
record.test_reason: Self-declared satire about benchmark contamination. Its 'grokking-like' canary-prediction curve is a joke figure. The model is trained on the test benchmarks themselves, so no held-out generalization is measured, and the author says the numbers may be made up. No version's behaviour is tested. Grokking papers are cited only to set up the joke.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The author declares the manuscript satire and argues that benchmark claims are undermined by boastful results made without serious investigation of data contamination. No result is offered as a real empirical finding.
record.recipe_differences: Pretraining on academic evaluation benchmarks and measuring canary prediction; it does not reproduce the original small-algorithmic-dataset grokking setup.

fits_no_version.finding: The satirical Fig. 2 (right) shows a 'grokking-like' rise in canary-string output when the model is trained on contaminated benchmark data. It is not presented as a real result.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Apparent sudden capability gains in models pretrained on evaluation data may reflect memorization or contamination rather than generalization. This is a cautionary point, not an empirical finding.

record.problems: The manuscript explicitly identifies itself as satire and says its reported numbers may be made up. The canary result is shown only as a figure, with no numeric values or uncertainty. It reports no controls, and pretraining on the evaluation benchmarks makes the canary result unsuitable as evidence of generalization.
record.rows_left_out: The other benchmark performance, scaling, and contamination assertions are not separate rows for these claim versions; the text identifies the manuscript and its numbers as satire, and those assertions do not measure the versions' claimed behaviors.

untested.parts: No algorithmic dataset, train/test accuracy gap, or training-set-size comparison.
No non-algorithmic held-out generalization and no initialization or weight-norm manipulation.
No genuine pretraining or fine-tuning result. The 1M-parameter model is fictional satire.
No weight decay, efficiency, critical dataset size, or ungrokking result.
No comparison of algorithms across runs.

record.verdict_notes: Exclude this study from evidence on all versions. The record's relation and tranche (discusses/T6) are appropriate. The only change needed is the R1 state: change 'observed' to 'cannot_determine'.

versions.untested_parts: No small algorithmic dataset, training-versus-test accuracy trajectory, or training-set-size comparison.
No circuit or mechanism analysis, gradual circuit-formation measure, or memorizing-component removal.
The canary-prediction claim is not a test of delayed generalization on non-algorithmic data; no initialization-scale or weight-norm comparison is reported.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning result; the claimed model has 1 million parameters and the paper is satire.
No low-norm efficiency account, critical dataset size, or ungrokking result.
No comparison of learned algorithms across runs.

rows.subject: phi-CTNL
rows.operation_detail: Canary-prediction accuracy across pretraining epochs after pretraining on academic evaluation benchmarks
rows.note: The text describes grokking-like canary prediction, but does not give plotted values. The paper says it is satire and that its numbers might be made up; this is not a test of generalization because the evaluation benchmarks are used for pretraining.
rows.check: Recorded as 'observed', but this is not a measurement of delayed generalization. Canaries are memorized from the training data, which is the test set, and the figure is satirical and possibly fabricated (the Fig. 1 caption says numbers 'might have made them up'). The state should be cannot_determine, and the row arguably should not be a result row at all.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
